items.text: 22. V1 Acceptance Criteria
V1 acceptance: a seller can create a brand profile once.
V1 acceptance: a seller can reuse the brand profile across products.
V1 acceptance: a seller can provide apparel product information through a structured form.
V1 acceptance: a seller can provide apparel product information through bulk input.
V1 acceptance: the system can represent one style with multiple color/size variants.
V1 acceptance: every important canonical attribute can retain its source.
V1 acceptance: every important canonical attribute can retain its confidence.
V1 acceptance: the system can map one canonical product into marketplace-specific category/field structures.
V1 acceptance: the system can distinguish required, conditional, optional and unsupported fields.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate the title from verified product facts.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate bullets from verified product facts.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate the description from verified product facts.
V1 acceptance: the system can generate keywords from verified product facts.
V1 acceptance: the system can validate the product before submission.
V1 acceptance: the system can show blocking reasons from pre-submission validation.
V1 acceptance: the system can identify missing data.
V1 acceptance: the system can ask targeted human questions about missing data.
V1 acceptance: the system can submit a listing.
V1 acceptance: the system can record the submission attempt.
V1 acceptance: the system can read the resulting marketplace status/error.
V1 acceptance: the system can automatically fix defined deterministic error classes.
V1 acceptance: the system can retry safely without creating uncontrolled duplicate submissions.
V1 acceptance: the system can escalate unresolved issues to a human.
V1 acceptance: the system can confirm a listing as LIVE only after marketplace success confirmation.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show per-marketplace status.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show listing identifiers per marketplace.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show issues per marketplace.
V1 acceptance: the dashboard can show latest activity per marketplace.
V1 acceptance: the system preserves history so the team can understand what changed and why.
23. Product Metrics for V1
Table header: Metric | Definition
V1 metric "Time to first listing": time from complete product intake to first successful live listing.
V1 metric "Listing success rate": percentage of listing jobs that reach LIVE without manual marketplace intervention.
V1 metric "First-pass success rate": percentage of submissions accepted without a correction cycle.
V1 metric "Auto-resolution rate": percentage of errors resolved by the agent without seller intervention.
V1 metric "Human question rate": percentage of products requiring at least one seller question.
V1 metric "Average human questions per SKU": questions asked per product/job.
V1 metric "Error recurrence rate": percentage of issues that reappear after correction.
V1 metric "Duplicate submission rate": unwanted duplicate listing/submission incidents.
V1 metric "Attribute completeness": percentage of required/conditional fields correctly populated before submission.
V1 metric "Live confirmation accuracy": percentage of listings marked LIVE that are actually live.
24. Handoff to Lead Engineer: What Must Be Clear Before Build (the following points must be clear before build).
Canonical product is the source of truth.
Marketplace listings are derived representations of the canonical product.
Marketplace schemas are versioned.
Marketplace schemas can change.
Every field should have a source.
Critical facts should have confidence/evidence.
Required fields are marketplace + category + context dependent.
Variant relationships are first-class product data, not just a UI feature.
Listing status is per marketplace.
Listing status is per variant where necessary.
Errors are first-class records.
Error records carry a classification.
Error records carry a severity.
Error records carry a resolution state.
Human questions are first-class workflow tasks, not generic support tickets.
Every submission should be auditable.
Every correction should be auditable.
The workflow must be resumable.
If a seller answers one question, the agent continues from the blocked step rather than restarting the entire job.
The agent must be idempotent at the business level.
Repeated status checks should not create duplicate product identities.
Safe retries should not create duplicate product identities.
Preserve separation: the system should preserve marketplace-specific data.
Preserve separation: the canonical product should not be polluted with marketplace-only fields ("without polluting the canonical product with marketplace-only fields").
25. Open product decisions are to be locked before implementation.
Table header: Decision | Recommended V1 Decision to Discuss
Open decision "Exact marketplace launch order" (recommended V1, to discuss): pick 2–3 marketplaces for first production validation.
Open decision "Exact marketplace launch order" (recommended V1): add adapters incrementally.
Open decision "Seller input method" (recommended V1, to discuss): start with guided form.
Open decision "Seller input method" (recommended V1): start with spreadsheet upload.
Open decision "Seller input method" (recommended V1): add connected PIM/ERP after core workflow is stable.
Open decision "Human approval" (recommended V1, to discuss): default to autonomous submission after validation.
Open decision "Human approval" (recommended V1): optional approval mode for cautious sellers.
Open decision "Content language" (recommended V1, to discuss): start with English.
Open decision "Content language" (recommended V1): keep the content model language-ready.
Open decision "Image generation" (recommended V1, to discuss): do not make image generation a dependency for V1 listing completion.
Open decision "Marketplace schema refresh" (recommended V1, to discuss): treat schema/rules as versioned.
Open decision "Marketplace schema refresh" (recommended V1): treat schema/rules as refreshable rather than static.
Open decision "Error library" (recommended V1, to discuss): build an internal error taxonomy.
Open decision "Error library" (recommended V1): continuously map marketplace errors into the internal error taxonomy.
Open decision "Confidence threshold" (recommended V1, to discuss): define which attributes can be inferred.
Open decision "Confidence threshold" (recommended V1): define which attributes always require evidence/confirmation.
Open decision "Bulk listing" (recommended V1, to discuss): design for one SKU and bulk SKU jobs from the same underlying workflow.
26. Reference Basis
The product requirements above are intentionally marketplace-agnostic.
The listed official sources were used to ground the marketplace/compliance sections.
The official sources should be treated as external references, not as permanent hard-coded requirements.

Founder's Direct POV Document Status: V1 Product / Business Requirements.
Founder's Direct POV Document Status: Apparel Niche.
AUTONOMOUS LISTING AGENT
V1 Business Requirements & End-to-End Listing Process are for Apparel / Fashion Marketplace Sellers.
Important Notice on Living Marketplace Rules
Marketplace schemas change.
Marketplace required fields change.
Marketplace allowed values change.
Marketplace validation rules change.
The product must treat marketplace requirements as living rules rather than a one-time hard-coded field list.
Amazon explicitly provides marketplace/product-type schemas.
Amazon notes that requirements can change.
Flipkart states that listing rules are subject to change.
Purpose of this Document
Document purpose: define, in non-technical business language, exactly what the product must collect when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must understand when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must create when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must validate when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must submit when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must monitor when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must repair when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
Document purpose: define exactly what the product must report when a seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces.
A seller wants to publish an apparel SKU across marketplaces from one dashboard.

V1 product promise: seller gives basic brand + product information once.
V1 product promise: the agent turns seller information into marketplace-ready listings.
V1 product promise: the agent manages the listing lifecycle until the listing is live or a human decision is genuinely required.
Primary niche: Apparel / fashion products.
Primary user: D2C brands.
Primary user: manufacturers.
Primary user: traders.
Primary user: small sellers.
Primary user: marketplace agencies managing apparel catalogs.
Core outcome step 1 of 6: One product source of truth.

Core outcome step 4 of 6: submission (after validation).
Core outcome step 5 of 6: error resolution (after submission).
Core outcome step 6 of 6: live confirmation (after error resolution).
Operating principle: do not ask the seller for information the system can reliably derive, reuse or validate.
Operating principle: ask only when missing information materially blocks a correct listing.
1. Product in One Sentence
The Autonomous Listing Agent is a listing operations agent, not merely a content generator.
The Autonomous Listing Agent takes a seller's product information and assets.
The Autonomous Listing Agent builds a canonical product record.
The Autonomous Listing Agent maps that product to each marketplace's category and field structure.
The Autonomous Listing Agent generates or transforms listing content.
The Autonomous Listing Agent validates completeness.
The Autonomous Listing Agent validates compliance.
The Autonomous Listing Agent submits the listing.
The Autonomous Listing Agent reads marketplace responses.
The Autonomous Listing Agent fixes resolvable errors.
The Autonomous Listing Agent asks the seller only for unresolved information.
The Autonomous Listing Agent resubmits.
The Autonomous Listing Agent confirms the final live status.
2. The End-to-End Flow
The complete lifecycle from seller onboarding to live verification consists of 19 operational stages.
Stage 1 Seller / brand onboarding: capture stable business identity once.
Stage 1 Seller / brand onboarding: capture stable legal identity once.
Stage 1 Seller / brand onboarding: capture stable brand identity once.
Stage 1 Seller / brand onboarding: capture stable tax identity once.
Stage 2 Marketplace account connection: authenticate seller accounts.
Stage 2 Marketplace account connection: store IDs.
Stage 2 Marketplace account connection: store default commercial terms.
Stage 3 Product intake: multi-modal ingestion via forms.
Stage 3 Product intake: multi-modal ingestion via CSV.
Stage 3 Product intake: multi-modal ingestion via ERP.
Stage 3 Product intake: multi-modal ingestion of images.
Stage 3 Product intake: multi-modal ingestion of size charts.
Stage 4 Product understanding: isolate verified factual data from promotional marketing noise.
Stage 5 Category & sub-category classification: map gender into marketplace taxonomy.
Stage 5 Category & sub-category classification: map apparel type into marketplace taxonomy.
Stage 6 Attribute extraction & normalization: normalize fabric.
Stage 6 Attribute extraction & normalization: normalize fit.
Stage 6 Attribute extraction & normalization: normalize pattern.
Stage 6 Attribute extraction & normalization: normalize color.
Stage 6 Attribute extraction & normalization: normalize weave.
Stage 6 Attribute extraction & normalization: normalize care.
Stage 7 Canonical Product Intelligence record: create single source of truth record.
Stage 7: the Canonical Product Intelligence record is immutable.
Stage 8 Marketplace schema mapping: transform canonical facts into target marketplace schemas.
Stage 9 Content generation & optimization: generate titles.
Stage 9 Content generation & optimization: generate bullets.
Stage 9 Content generation & optimization: generate descriptions.
Stage 9 Content generation & optimization: generate search keywords.
Stage 10 Media and variant validation: validate size charts.
Stage 10 Media and variant validation: validate swatch shots.
Stage 10 Media and variant validation: validate parent-child links.
Stage 11 Compliance & completeness validation: pre-flight checks against Legal Metrology 2022.
Stage 11 Compliance & completeness validation: pre-flight checks against portal rules.
Stage 12 Human clarification only where necessary: targeted single-question prompts for blocking gaps.
Stage 13 Marketplace submission: dispatch validated payloads to marketplace APIs.
Stage 14 Submission/status monitoring: asynchronous polling for feed outcomes.
Stage 14 Submission/status monitoring: webhook listeners for feed outcomes.
Stage 15 Error diagnosis: translate raw portal error codes into plain actionable language.
Stage 16 Automatic correction: auto-fix deterministic enum mismatches.
Stage 16 Automatic correction: auto-fix deterministic formatting (source: "enum mismatches, formatting & sizing").
Stage 16 Automatic correction: auto-fix deterministic sizing (source: "enum mismatches, formatting & sizing").
Stage 17 Resubmission: safe bounded retry.
Stage 17 Resubmission: retry with updated payload.
Stage 17 Resubmission: retry with incremented attempt.
Stage 18 Live confirmation: capture live URL.
Stage 18 Live confirmation: capture marketplace SKU.
Stage 18 Live confirmation: capture ASIN/FSN.
Stage 18 Live confirmation: capture active state.
Stage 19 Dashboard status + audit history: show unified multi-marketplace operational view.
Stage 19 Dashboard status + audit history: show audit trail.
3. V1 Scope and Non-Goals
Definition of Success
A product is not considered 'listed' merely because a submission was sent.
A product is successful only when the marketplace confirms the relevant SKU/listing is live/active.
Success also requires the dashboard can show the marketplace identifier.
Success also requires the dashboard can show the current status.
Success also requires the dashboard can show the latest validation state.

4. Marketplace Strategy
V1 should be designed around a common apparel product model.
V1 should be designed around marketplace-specific adapters, alongside ("plus") the common apparel product model.
The common model is the source of truth.
Each marketplace adapter decides which fields are required, optional or conditionally required.
Each marketplace adapter decides allowed values.
Each marketplace adapter decides formatting rules.
Each marketplace adapter decides variation rules.
Each marketplace adapter decides submission/status behavior.
Target marketplace set can include Amazon.
Target marketplace set can include Flipkart.
Target marketplace set can include Myntra.
Target marketplace set can include AJIO.
Target marketplace set can include Meesho.
Target marketplace set can include Nykaa Fashion.
Target marketplace set is subject to the commercial/API access available to the business.
Category Semantic Variance: do not assume that the same apparel category means the same thing on every marketplace.
No Hard-Coded Lists: do not hard-code a single universal 'required fields' list.
Dynamic Schemas: for each connected marketplace, maintain a current marketplace/category schema.
Dynamic Schemas: map the canonical product into each connected marketplace/category schema.
Amazon: Product Type Definitions are the source for product-type and marketplace requirements, including required/conditional attributes.
Flipkart Listing Management documentation separates product information from the seller listing.
Flipkart states listing rules can change.
Because listing rules can change, errors should be handled explicitly (Flipkart Listing Management documentation).

5. Brand Onboarding: Information to Collect Once
Onboarding should be designed so that the seller enters stable information once.
The agent reuses onboarding information across products.
The agent reuses onboarding information across marketplaces.
5.1 Brand / Business Profile
Table header: Field / Group | What to Collect | Why it Matters
Brand profile field "Legal business name": registered business name; matters for account and compliance identity.
Brand profile field "Brand name(s)": exact consumer-facing brand name(s); matters for listing brand identity.
Brand profile field "Brand owner type": Brand owner / manufacturer / reseller / distributor / trader.
Brand owner type changes product identity and proof requirements.
Brand profile field "Brand website": website/store URL; reference source for product facts.
Brand profile field "Brand description": short factual brand description; used as content context.
Brand profile field "Brand logo": primary logo assets; for branding / media where supported.
Brand profile field "Brand registry / authorization": marketplace-specific status where relevant.
Brand registry / authorization: supporting proof where relevant; matters for brand-related listing permissions.
Brand profile field "Customer care": email.
Brand profile field "Customer care": phone.
Brand profile field "Customer care": support details; matters for compliance and seller-facing information.
Brand profile field "Registered address": business address; matters for compliance / marketplace account information.
Brand profile field "Manufacturer details": manufacturer name.
Brand profile field "Manufacturer details": manufacturer address; matters for apparel/product declarations.
Brand profile field "Packer / importer details": packer details, where applicable; matters for compliance.
Brand profile field "Packer / importer details": importer details, where applicable; matters for compliance.
Brand profile field "Country of origin": country of manufacture/origin; matters for compliance and listing.
Brand profile field "GST / tax information": seller-provided tax details; matters for marketplace setup and tax-related fields.
Brand profile field "GST / tax information": applicable registrations.
5.2 Marketplace Account Profile
Table header: Field / Group | Collect
Marketplace account field "Marketplace": marketplace name.
Marketplace account field "Seller account": connected seller account / store identifier.
Marketplace account field "Seller display name": marketplace-facing seller/store name.
Marketplace account field "Pickup / fulfillment locations": locations relevant to the seller.
Marketplace account field "Default shipping / procurement settings": where the marketplace requires them.
Marketplace account field "Listing permissions": brand/category permissions, approvals or restrictions.
Marketplace account field "Identifier status": GTIN/EAN/UPC availability or exemption status, as applicable.
Marketplace account field "Default commercial rules": default MRP, where applicable.
Default commercial rules: selling price, where applicable.
Default commercial rules: tax/HSN conventions, where applicable.
Default commercial rules: shipping or SLA inputs, where applicable.
5.3 Seller Catalog Intake Options
The seller should be able to provide product information in multiple ways.
Catalog intake option: single product form.
Catalog intake option: bulk spreadsheet/template upload.
Catalog intake option: images + basic product information.
Catalog intake option: existing catalog export.
Catalog intake option: ERP/PIM/catalog source, where available.
Catalog intake option: URL/website product page, where permitted.
Catalog intake option: combination of the above.
Data Ingestion Rule
Data Ingestion Rule: the system should merge intake inputs rather than forcing the seller to repeat information.
